items.title: Show HN: Orrery, a Three.js solar system visualization powered by real NAIF data
items.contentSnippet:
Hi HN, I'm excited to share a personal project that I've put a lot of love into.
This is Orrery[0], a Three.js-based visualization of our solar system. It allows the positions of the major bodies to be played and scrubbed through the years 1950 - 2050, with optional orbit path displays and various other visualization options.
The data comes from NAIF SPICE - a framework and set of open-source data kernels containing highly detailed space geometry data.

items.title: Show HN: Digital scarcity; app where photos gradually decay with time / views
items.contentSnippet:
Like instagram, but all photos have a shelf life: they can be up for year, an hour or ten minutes, or up until they're viewed 100 times, 1000 times or a million times, etc.
The longer they're up, the more they fade - user chosen filters are applied gradually over the lifetime of the photo (be it measured in clicks or time), gradually obscuring it. At the end of its lifetime, the pictures faded / expired, and disappears, though comments remain.

items.title: Show HN: Shlexball, describe a file and a local 1.5B model finds it on your Mac
items.contentSnippet:
Basically, I didn't want to waste my opus 5.5 or codex Astra credits just to find files in my machine, so I trained a local LLM which is only 1.5B to write bash to find files on your macos laptop (works on apple silicon, uses little ram).
Full privacy since it's local so you can look for your sensitive files and api keys without sending them to a third party server.

items.title: Show HN: Every click on this page draws a new Maurer rose
items.contentSnippet:
Hi HN, this is a small click counter. Each click on the page increments a global count, and the new count n draws a rose.
It runs on a 2012 MacBook Air with Debian, nginx and a ~20-line PHP script that takes a file lock, behind a Cloudflare Tunnel. The counter is an 8-byte binary file.
